description: Retained-mode terminal UI framework for .NET 10 with mutable controls, deterministic layout and input, Unicode-aware rendering, styling, dialogs, windows, and managed console hosting.
releaseNotes: SharpVision 1.6.0-beta.7 prerelease: the last Turbo Vision gaps close through the theme model - GlyphFamily gains a Desktop glyph a Screen tiles across the application-window plane (a space everywhere but the classic family, whose ▒ is Borland's dithered TDeskTop, showing through transparent panels); a default Button (IsDefault) is presented in the Current visual state so styles.button.current can mark it (Turbo Vision's bright-cyan caption); a RadioButton's checked accent is now a code-owned default that yields to an authored styles.toggle.checked foreground; and the Turbo Vision theme maps muted to cyan so scrollbar rails read as Borland's shaded cyan track under a blue thumb. Since 1.6.0-beta.6, in which the theme vocabulary grew from six to ten presentation roles - "button" (ButtonStyle, now a well-known root in SharpVision.Styling), "toggle", "item", and "panel" - each cascading from its parent role until a theme authors it, Face gained a per-face AccessKeyColor channel a caption inherits from its owner, the theme's attributes.hotkey decoration replaced the hard-coded mnemonic underline, and Turbo Vision took Borland's green buttons with block shadows, cyan clusters and list viewers, borderless blue input line, per-plane access keys, and transparent groups. Since 1.6.0-beta.5, in which the Turbo Vision theme took its gray menu strip with red access keys, gray dialogs with a white active frame and green close mark, green selection, and blue accent. Since 1.6.0-beta.4, in which the Turbo Vision theme started following Borland's cpAppColor/cpGrayDialog roles on the CGA palette (blue desktop, gray dialogs with a white active frame, green selection, black lines and shadows, [X]/(•) marks through the "classic" glyph family), a Screen paints the theme's application-window plane so a desktop color shows without a hand-authored root face, a menu bar heading insets its caption by one cell on each side so the highlight reads " File ", and menu boxes and dialogs paint their frame cells on their own plane. Since 1.6.0-beta.2, in which menu bars started to behave like desktop menu bars - a drop-down hanging off a bar hosted above other content paints its own Bar plane and popup frame instead of showing that content through its rows (an IsAppearanceBoundary ends a continuous background plane), Up/Down in a drop-down move the cursor without opening submenu rows or trapping focus in a child, a closed submenu forgets its cursor and closes its nested branches leaf-first so reopening never resurrects a stale highlight, a hover-opened submenu shows no cursor until a row inside it is picked, and closing the chain returns focus to the control that owned it before the menu was entered. An application now holds at most one non-empty text selection: selecting in one owner collapses every other owner's range. Since 1.6.0-beta.1, which opened the control-authoring surface so a foreign control family can be built on the same seams the shipped controls use - new authoring bases (ScrollableCompositeControlBase, NumericInputBase, TemporalInputBase, ChartControlBase, FileDialogBase, ItemCollection<TItem>) and ControlBase capabilities for press and drag gestures, owned drop-down popups, modal sessions, owner-bound timers (ControlTimer), and glyph resolution, with the ItemsControl, InputBase, Container, and FloatingSurfaceBase pipeline hooks published rather than internal. Also fixes layout and scrolling correctness (Overlay navigation-slot walking, Container popup and BringIntoView arrangement coherence, monotone scrollbar reservations, ArrangeUniformRows offset remapping, Percent/Star lengths rebased against Viewport), selection integrity (spurious TabControl/Table events, in-flight proposals invalidated on batched structural changes), word-wrap trailing whitespace with O(log n) word navigation, and culture-invariant geometry and layout formatting. See https://github.com/pavkam/sharp-vision/blob/main/docs/index.md for API contracts, examples, and current support.
